hook.text: Legend says a nomad stored milk in a goat-skin bag. Body heat fermented it by evening. Yogurt was born by accident.

buildup.text: Yogurt requires two specific bacteria: Streptococcus thermophilus and Lactobacillus bulgaricus. They work as a team.

discovery.text: Streptococcus starts fast, producing acid and CO₂. Lactobacillus finishes slow, deepening flavor and thickening texture.

twist.text: Greek yogurt is regular yogurt strained to remove whey. It takes 3 cups of milk to make 1 cup of Greek yogurt.

climax.text: The yogurt industry generates millions of tons of acid whey as waste. Finding uses for it is a major environmental challenge.

punchline.text: Two bacteria, warm milk, and a few hours. Simple recipe, complex science.

quiz.question: Which two bacteria are essential for yogurt making?
